# `session_choice_label`: `Chan.choose` with a label the protocol does not offer

At a `choose` step, `Chan.choose(ch, :label)` picks one of the protocol's
branches. The label must be an atom literal naming one of those branches. A
label the protocol does not list, or a label that is not an atom literal, is
this error.

## A program that triggers it

```march
mod Main do
  type Client = Client
  type Server = Server

  protocol Lookup do
    choose by Server:
      ok  -> Server -> Client : Int
      err -> Server -> Client : String
    end
  end

  fn main() do
    let (cc, sc) = Chan.new(Lookup)
    let sc2 = Chan.choose(sc, :found)
    Chan.close(Chan.send(sc2, 7))
    let (lbl, cc2) = Chan.offer(cc)
    match lbl do
      :ok ->
        let (_n, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
      :err ->
        let (_msg, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
    end
  end
end
```

`Lookup` offers `:ok` and `:err`. There is no `:found` branch.

## The fix

Choose one of the branches the protocol declares:

```march
mod Main do
  type Client = Client
  type Server = Server

  protocol Lookup do
    choose by Server:
      ok  -> Server -> Client : Int
      err -> Server -> Client : String
    end
  end

  fn main() do
    let (cc, sc) = Chan.new(Lookup)
    let sc2 = Chan.choose(sc, :ok)
    Chan.close(Chan.send(sc2, 7))
    let (lbl, cc2) = Chan.offer(cc)
    match lbl do
      :ok ->
        let (_n, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
      :err ->
        let (_msg, cc3) = Chan.recv(cc2)
        Chan.close(cc3)
    end
  end
end
```

## Why the rule exists

The label is what tells the peer which branch follows. A label the peer
has no branch for would leave it unable to continue. The label must also be a
literal so the compiler knows which branch's steps the channel follows next.

See also: [choice: `choose` and `offer`](../session-types.md#choice-choose-and-offer).
